name: Tactile push button 6 x 6 mm, through-hole, 4 legs
description: Momentary push button: pressing it connects its two contacts, letting go opens them. Four legs in a 6.5 x 4.5 mm rectangle; each leg is joined inside to the leg straight across the body (6.5 mm), and the two legs on the same side (4.5 mm) are the switch. On an ESP32: one contact to a GPIO, the other to GND, with the pin's internal pull-up on (pressed reads 0).
maker: unknown (generic, the common 6 x 6 mm size)

identified.how: from the kit photo (SW1, SW2, SW3, SW5 next to the ESP32) and the owner's photo of a loose one with a drawing of which legs switch (photos/top_and_pinout.jpg, 2026-11-19): current in at one leg and out at the other leg on the same side

mounting: through-hole: four legs, two on each of two opposite sides

footprint.name: TACT_SWITCH_6X6
footprint.why: pads 1 and 2 are the two legs on one side (4.5 mm apart, the switch); 3 and 4 the legs on the other side, 6.5 mm across. Pin 1 is pads 1 and 3 (joined inside), pin 2 is pads 2 and 4. Drill 1.0 mm, the usual hole for these legs

legs.source: the common 6 x 6 mm tact switch (6.5 mm across the body, 4.5 mm along a side); the owner's photo, scaled by the 6 mm body, agrees (about 4.4 mm along a side); not measured with calipers

body.source: the size the part is sold as; the owner's photo agrees

height.source: not known: these come with plungers from 4.3 to 13 mm above the board; measure before the box

pin_numbering: pin 1 is the two legs of one contact (pads 1 and 3, straight across the body); pin 2 the other contact (pads 2 and 4)
pins: one contact: to the GPIO (with its pull-up on)

status.symbol: 2026-11-19: placed in a schematic in Fusion 2706.1.17, pins 1 and 2 wired and read back (Fusion labels each 1*2 / 2*2: one pin on two pads), looked at (fusion/symbol.png)
